core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base (proof lines 2144-2168): given a base change of the whole situation along a morphism from an affine scheme, refine the covering of that base change by a finite etale covering by affines; restricting the given isomorphisms along the induced morphisms exhibits the same shape of data over the refinement, so the problem reduces to the case of an affine base.

Reduce to a single covering morphism (proof lines 2168-2188): in the affine case the covering may be replaced by one surjective etale morphism of affines, first by passing to a finite subcovering and then by taking the disjoint union; the data then consists of an isomorphism over the base change of the pair to the covering of the base.

Compare and descend (proof lines 2188-2226): the standard relative dualizing complex pulls back to the same object, and by uniqueness there is a unique isomorphism between the two; combining with the given isomorphism produces a comparison over the covering, whose two pullbacks to the double covering agree again by uniqueness; since negative self extensions vanish and this remains true after pullback, the descent result for objects with vanishing negative self extensions gives the required isomorphism on the source.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an affine base by refining the covering.
Replace the covering by a single surjective etale morphism of affines.
Build the comparison over the covering and descend it using vanishing of negative self extensions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a pair on a proper flat morphism of finite presentation is a relative dualizing complex as soon as its restriction to an affine etale covering of the base is isomorphic to the standard pair (statement lines 2140-2157). The proof (proof lines 2158-2226) reduces to an affine base and a single covering morphism, constructs the comparison isomorphism over the covering, verifies agreement on the double cover by uniqueness, and descends using the vanishing of negative self extensions. H3: a multi stage descent argument written out in full.
